{{Short description|Dutch-Israeli theoretical physicist (1929–2025)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2025}}
[[File:Avraham_Rinat.jpg|thumb|Rinat in 2023]]
'''Avraham S. Rinat-Reiner''' ({{Langx|he|אברהם רינת}}; 3 June 1929 – September 2025) was a Dutch-Israeli theoretical physicist who worked as professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/particle/content/avraham-s-rinat |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190809170130/http://www.weizmann.ac.il/particle/content/avraham-s-rinat |title=Avraham S. Rinat |publisher=Weizmann Institute of Science |date= |archive-date=9 August 2019}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Rinat was born in [[Amsterdam]] on 3 June 1929.<ref name="KaaKaa2008">{{cite book|author1=D. J. van de Kaa|author2=Kaa|author3=Y. de Roo|title=De Leden Van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie Van Wetenschappen: Een Demografisch Perspectief: 1808 Tot 2008|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gzNvCGJEGCYC&pg=PA329|date=19 December 2008|publisher=Amsterdam University Press|isbn=978-90-6984-552-4|page=329}}</ref> During his childhood he was friends with [[Anne Frank]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e8WU88xOOpI |title=Avraham Rinat – Anne Frank Fonds |publisher=Anne Frank Fonds Basel via YouTube |date=2 May 2019 |access-date=14 June 2020}}</ref> During World War II Rinat went into hiding on a farm in [[Hollandscheveld]]. He ended up in [[Westerbork transit camp]] where he remained until the liberation of the camp.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.ushmm.org/online/hsv/person_view.php?PersonId=4999040 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200614182940/https://www.ushmm.org/online/hsv/person_view.php?PersonId=4999040 |title=Avraham Rinat |publisher=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum |date= |archive-date=14 June 2020}}</ref> In 1958 he obtained his PhD at the [[University of Amsterdam]] under professor J. de Boer with a thesis titled: "Structure effects in the interaction between nuclei and atomic electrons".<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.albumacademicum.uva.nl/cgi/b/bib/bib-idx?type=simple;lang=nl;c=ap;rgn1=entirerecord;q1=Reiner;x=0;y=0;cc=ap;view=reslist;sort=achternaam;fmt=long;page=reslist;start=1;size=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200614184821/http://www.albumacademicum.uva.nl/cgi/b/bib/bib-idx?type=simple;lang=nl;c=ap;rgn1=entirerecord;q1=Reiner;x=0;y=0;cc=ap;view=reslist;sort=achternaam;fmt=long;page=reslist;start=1;size=1 |title=A.S. Reiner, 1929 - |language=Dutch |publisher=University of Amsterdam |date= |archive-date=14 June 2020}}</ref>

He was elected a corresponding member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1981.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4703 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427155834/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4703 |title=Avraham Rinat-Reiner |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=27 April 2020}}</ref>

Rinat died in September 2025, at the age of 96.<ref>{{Cite web |title=רינת אברהם |url=https://kdr.org.il/deceased/%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%A0%D7%AA-%D7%90%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%94%D7%9D/ |access-date=22 September 2025 |website=חברה קדישא רחובות |language=he-IL}}</ref>
